latin: Quicquid dicant caeteri cabalistae, ego decem spheras sic decem numerationibus correspondere dico, ut ab aedificio incipiendo, Iupiter sit quartae, Mars quintae, Sol sextae, Saturnus septimae, Venus octauae, Mercurius nonae, Luna decimae; tum supra aedificium, firmamentum tertiae, Primum mobile secundae, caelum empyreum decimae.
latin_note: Farmer's own English marks the terminal clause '[sic]' ("the empyrean heaven to the tenth [sic]", farmer1998:27474), signalling an apparent inconsistency (the tenth numeration has already been assigned to the moon). Akopyan's transcription of the same clause reads 'celum Empyreum prima' (the empyrean heaven corresponds to the first) rather than 'decimae' (akopyan2018:743; akopyan2021:1455), which would resolve the inconsistency, but this variant reading is not confirmed against Farmer's own edition apparatus.
translation: Whatever the other Cabalists say, I hold that the ten spheres correspond to the ten numerations in this way: starting from the edifice, Jupiter to the fourth, Mars to the fifth, the Sun to the sixth, Saturn to the seventh, Venus to the eighth, Mercury to the ninth, the Moon to the tenth; then, above the edifice, the firmament to the third, the Primum Mobile to the second, and the empyrean heaven to the tenth.
translation_note: 'numerationibus' = the sefirot. 'aedificio'/'aedificium' ('the edifice') is a Kabbalistic term Farmer glosses as 'the fourth through tenth sefirot' (paraphrase; farmer1998:27453, cross-referring to 28.9). The terminal 'caelum empyreum decimae' is translated as printed in the packet's Farmer-sourced Latin, though see latin_note on a variant reading.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-swarm-batch3, from Latin at farmer1998:27423
doctrine: Thesis 11>48 correlates the ten celestial spheres of Ptolemaic cosmology with the ten sefirot, against 'whatever the other Cabalists say' (farmer1998:27423). Farmer's note glosses 'numerations' as the sefirot and 'edifice' as the fourth through tenth sefirot (paraphrase; farmer1998:27453), and reports that Wirszubski (1989) read Pico's 'inferior chariot' of the companion thesis 11>50 as 'a symbol of a lower triad of the ten sefirot' and 'an example of magical use of the sefirot system', while Farmer counters that Pico's own thesis 11>22 (printed in the source OCR as '1122', per this packet's stated digit convention for '>') defines the 'inferior chariot' as the realm of 'sensible natures' (paraphrase; farmer1998:27453).
context: Farmer's cross-reference apparatus ties the thesis to 11>2, Pico's fourfold division of speculative Kabbala (farmer1998:26383); to 11>49, on the correspondence of the ten commandments to the numerations (farmer1998:27430); to 11>50, on the 'inferior chariot' (farmer1998:27439); and to 28.9 and 28.22 on the 'edifice' and the chariots (farmer1998:17649, 17959).
reception: Dougherty groups the thesis under a specific rubric: "Among the Kabbalistic theses with magical themes are four that dealt with astrology" (dougherty2008:7890), of which 11>48 is the first cited. Akopyan quotes the thesis's correspondence scheme in both of his studies of Pico and astrology (akopyan2018:743; akopyan2021:1455), and Howlett and Busi and Ebgi likewise quote its Latin in full (howlett2021:7774; busi2014:24617). A German study of Pico's kabbalistic paradigm pairs the thesis with 11>66 as together illustrating the linkage of soul-faculties and planetary spheres to the sefirotic pattern (paraphrase; kabbalah_paradigma:1566).
historiography: Dougherty situates 11>48 within a set of four astrological-Kabbalistic theses with 'magical themes' (dougherty2008:7890). Akopyan's two transcriptions of the thesis's final clause diverge from the Farmer-sourced text used here (see latin_note), a divergence not resolved in the sources consulted.

quotations.text: Among the Kabbalistic theses with magical themes are four that dealt with astrology

not_established: Whether the Farmer-sourced 'caelum empyreum decimae' or Akopyan's 'celum Empyreum prima' is the more accurate transcription of Pico's printed text is not established from the sources consulted.
The full content of Farmer's cross-reference to thesis 11>22 ('sensible natures') was not independently read; only the paraphrase at farmer1998:27453 was consulted.
